headline: EU Commission reported to scrap Green Claims proposal; repairability consultation opens
summary: Reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon the proposed Green Claims Directive, potentially easing ex-ante verification burdens for environmental marketing. Meanwhile, a new Commission consultation on product repairability directly targets consumer durables. Legal analysis also confirmed your CSRD obligations for FY2027 while keeping you outside direct CSDDD scope.

items.title: Commission reported to withdraw Green Claims Directive proposal
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission intends to drop the proposed Green Claims Directive and its third-party pre-verification scheme for environmental claims.
items.meaning: Ex-ante substantiation requirements for product environmental claims may be shelved, though general anti-greenwashing rules under the Empowering Consumers Directive remain applicable to tool packaging.
items.action: Monitor official Commission updates before modifying ongoing environmental claim substantiation processes.

sources.title: Commission confirms plans to scrap Green Claims Directive
EU Commission Scraps Green Claims Directive

items.title: Commission opens public consultation on product repairability rules
items.what: The European Commission launched a public consultation seeking feedback on potential EU measures to improve product repairability and reduce waste.
items.meaning: Future rules could directly impact design standards, spare part availability, and technical documentation for power tools and garden equipment manufactured by Chinese suppliers.
items.action: Review product repairability design criteria and consider contributing feedback to the Commission consultation.

sources.title: Commission launches public consultation on making products easier to repair
EU launches consultation on tougher repairability rules to cut waste

items.title: Omnibus reform analysis details revised CSRD and CSDDD thresholds
items.what: Published legal analysis outlines modified corporate reporting and due diligence obligations following the EU Omnibus reform package.
items.meaning: Confirms your business remains subject to CSRD reporting from financial year 2027 while remaining outside the direct scope of CSDDD due to headcount.
items.action: Maintain supply chain ESG data collection planning with mainland Chinese suppliers for FY2027 reporting.
